snippet.text: `Lowering` holds one proposal against the fence, and `refusal()` says why it fails. It refuses a decision-model executor, a refuted verdict, a `melian/injection-attempt` claim, and a defect a deterministic check co-reported. It refuses a P0, a target of `nit`, and any move but one step down. It refuses a target the table in force resolves `silent`, a table Melian could not read, and a proposal with no evidence at the head. `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` says why a later report of a claim cannot follow the stored one: it is taken only when none is stored, when it is the stored report again, as a replay sends it, or when its verdict is stronger, and it then replaces the stored report whole. Otherwise the first report stands, its reason and lowering included, as [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) sets out.
